ai_summary:
Great Britain is currently generating 13.8 GW of total wind output, with estimated Scottish wind output delivering 3.1 GW, representing 30.7% of installed Scottish wind capacity. This high renewable penetration maintains a Scottish carbon intensity of 0 gCO2/kWh, in stark contrast to 62 gCO2/kWh GB-wide. However, cross-border transmission constraints continue to bottleneck this abundant clean power. Consequently, 21.5 GWh of Scottish generation has been curtailed so far today through Balancing Mechanism bids at a direct constraint cost of about £484,058. Replacing this stranded green energy required an estimated 4,085,095 m3 of fossil gas to be burned elsewhere on the network, needlessly adding 7,525 tonnes of CO2 to the atmosphere. 

Extrapolating today’s constraint figures indicates an estimated total yearly curtailment cost of £177 million. When smeared across national grid balancing mechanisms, this system friction is estimated to increase electricity invoices by roughly £0.6/MWh for consumers across the UK. These figures highlight an ongoing operational inefficiency where zero-carbon Scottish generation is routinely discarded at substantial financial and environmental expense, reinforcing the critical necessity of accelerating north-to-south transmission grid upgrades.
